sentences.text: The order impugned is an order passed by adjudicating officer referable to Section 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
The said order is clearly appealable before the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal under Section 70(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner states that Tribunal has been constituted and is functioning.

sentences.text: In view of that preliminary objection raised by Sri Piyush Srivastava, learned Standing Counsel for the State-respondents, interference claimed in exercise of extraordinary jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is declined.

4. However, keeping mind facts and circumstances of the case, specially in the present facts where entire action is described as contrary to the law, without entering into the merits and without making any observations as to the facts, the writ petition is disposed of with the direction subject to the petitioner's availing his statutory remedy of appeal before the Tribunal within a period of two weeks from today, that appeal may be entertain and decided on its own merits, in accordance with law, without being prejudiced any observation made by this Court in this order.
5. Further subject to the petitioner filing such appeal accompany with stay application, coercive measures may not be pursed against the petitioner for a period of one month.
All further actions shall abide by further order to be passed by the Tribunal.
